answer: Rule: a new identity activates only when an established insurer underwrites it with 100 units collateral. A proven fake pays victims from that collateral; the insurer loses its licence after two failures. One fake risks 100 units, ten fakes 1,000, and each insurer caps five identities per operator, so a ring must fool many underwriters. This haven stays open to saffron growers and timber haulers because fraud is priced in advance.
